mainTopic: Carrying out a dead person's instructions, children's transactions, and a husband's vows restricting his wife
overview: The amud opens by finishing אילפא's answer. Our משנה, where a שליש must carry out a dead father's instructions, follows רבי מאיר, who holds it is a מצוה to fulfill a dead person's words. רב חסדא, quoting מר עוקבא, then rules that a father's sons get all they need, whether he said 'give' a shekel or 'do not give' more. The גמרא explains that the father really wants them provided for and only meant to make them careful with money. Next, רפרם limits the משנה in גיטין that young children's deals in movable goods count: this applies only when they have no אפוטרופוס. He proves it from our משנה's words 'the action of a קטנה is nothing.' With that, פרק מציאת האשה ends. The new פרק opens with a משנה about a husband who makes a נדר restricting his wife: no benefit from him, no tasting a certain fruit, or no adorning herself. Each case can require him to divorce her and pay her כתובה, with time limits that differ by opinion. The גמרא then asks how his נדר can work if he already owes her support. It begins to answer that he can tell her to feed herself from her own earnings, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אילפא's answer: the משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: אילפא finds the ברייתא's ruling in our משנה. The משנה of the שליש who must carry out the father's instructions follows רבי מאיר, who holds it is a מצוה to carry out the instructions of someone who has died.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי מאיר, who says: it is a מצוה to fulfill the words of the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes אילפא's answer to a challenge that came from a ברייתא. He says the ruling follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that if a father ordered 'do not give my sons more than a shekel,' we give only a shekel, even if they need more. אילפא was challenged to find this in a משנה. He pointed to our משנה, where the שליש must carry out the dead father's instructions for his daughter. That משנה is רבי מאיר, who holds we must carry out a dead person's words, and the same principle is the source of the ברייתא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a מצוה to carry out the instructions of a person who has died
'It is' (this ruling is the opinion of...)

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Meir,
who says: it is a מצוה to fulfill the words of the dead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the challenge-and-answer exchange from the previous section (the ברייתא posed to אילפא).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the source to a specific תנא (רבי מאיר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'give only a shekel' ruling seemed to have no basis in our משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It follows רבי מאיר's rule that we must carry out a dead person's words.

steps.title: The הלכה: the sons get all they need
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting מר עוקבא, rules that whether the father said 'give' or 'do not give' more than a shekel, the sons receive everything they need.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of מר עוקבא: The הלכה is that whether he said 'give' or 'do not give,' we give them all they need.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא states the practical הלכה in the name of מר עוקבא: the sons always get all they need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling goes against the ברייתא, which said that if the father said 'do not give more than a shekel,' they get only a shekel. According to מר עוקבא, the father's wording makes no difference, and the sons are fully supported either way.

keyTerms.meaning: The final practical law
'Give!' (give my sons a shekel)
'Do not give!' (do not give more than a shekel)
All of their needs

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Mar Ukva said:
The halacha is: whether he said "Give"
phrases.notes: He means the father said 'give my sons a shekel a week.'

phrases.english: or whether he said "Do not give"
phrases.notes: Meaning 'do not give them more than a shekel.'

phrases.english: we give them all their needs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling that disagrees with the ברייתא just explained as following רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The father's sons receive all their needs no matter how he phrased his limit.

steps.title: Challenge: don't we follow רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we can ignore the father's words, since the הלכה follows רבי מאיר that we must carry out a dead person's words.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we hold that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר, who says it is a מצוה to fulfill the words of the dead!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges מר עוקבא's ruling. If the הלכה follows רבי מאיר, we should obey a father who said 'do not give more than a shekel.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question has two parts that clash: the accepted rule that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר, and מר עוקבא's ruling that ignores what the father said. Giving the sons more than he allowed seems to break the מצוה of carrying out his words.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But we hold that...', which introduces an accepted rule used as a challenge
The הלכה follows (this opinion)

phrases.aramaic: הָא קַיְימָא לַן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: But we hold that the halacha is like Rabbi Meir,
who says: it is a מצוה to fulfill the words of the dead?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of מר עוקבא in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר עוקבא's ruling that the sons get all they need even when the father said 'do not give.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר that a dead person's words must be carried out, so the father's limit should be obeyed.

steps.title: Answer: the father really wants them provided for
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר's rule applies to other matters. Here the father is happy for his sons to have what they need, and he only spoke to push them to be careful with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies to other matters. But here it is surely pleasing to him that they be provided for. And the reason he said this was to push them to be careful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Carrying out the father's words does not apply here, because he did not truly mean to hold his sons back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's rule is about carrying out what the dead person really wants. Here we can assume the father wants his sons properly supported, so his words were never a real limit. He said them only to push his sons to spend carefully.

keyTerms.meaning: 'These words apply...', which limits a rule to certain cases
Other matters
It is surely pleasing to him
To push them, to make them careful

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר that we carry out a dead person's words. Still, when a father limits support for his sons, they get all they need, because we assume he only meant to make them careful, not to deprive them.

phrases.english: These words apply in other matters,
but in this case it is surely pleasing to him,
phrases.notes: He means the father is happy for his sons to have everything they need.

phrases.english: and the fact that he said this —
he came only to push them to be careful.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the rule by reading the father's true intent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר's rule should force us to obey the father's spending limit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule still holds, but here the father's true wish is full support. His words were only meant to make the sons careful.

steps.title: משנה: young children's deals with movable goods count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in גיטין: young children's purchases and sales of movable property are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: young children's purchases are valid purchases and their sales are valid sales, with movable property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a משנה from another מסכת about young children doing business. It is setting up a ruling of רפרם that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that young children's buying and selling counts, but only for movable goods, not land. This is the base text that רפרם is about to limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Young children
A purchase
A sale
Movable property

steps.confusionAlert: This is a brand-new topic. It is not connected to the father's instructions about his sons in the steps before it.

phrases.english: We learned there:
Young children: their purchase is a purchase
and their sale is a sale, with movable property.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Young children's purchases and sales of movable goods are valid.

steps.title: רפרם: only when there is no guardian
steps.stepSummary: רפרם limits the משנה: young children's deals count only when they have no guardian. If they have one, their purchases and sales do not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם said: They taught this only when there is no guardian there. But if there is a guardian, their purchase is not a purchase and their sale is not a sale.
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם narrows the משנה just quoted. It applies only to children who have no guardian.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seemed to make young children's deals valid in all cases. רפרם limits it: if a guardian (אפוטרופוס) is in charge of their affairs, their purchases and sales do not count, even with movable goods.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They taught this only...', which limits a teaching to a certain case
A guardian who manages someone's affairs

phrases.english: Rafram said: They taught this only
where there is no guardian there,
but if there is a guardian there —
their purchase is not a purchase,
and their sale is not a sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Young children's deals with movable goods count only when they have no guardian.

steps.title: Where רפרם learned his rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רפרם's source and points to our משנה: 'the action of a קטנה is nothing.'
steps.simpleTranslation: From where does רפרם know this? From the fact that our משנה teaches: the action of a young girl is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רפרם got his rule that a child with a guardian cannot buy or sell. It answers that he learned it from a line in our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה dealt with a girl whose money was held by a שליש, and it said her own actions count for nothing. רפרם reads this as proof that when a child has someone in charge of her affairs, her deals do not count.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? What is the source?
Since it teaches (in the משנה)
A young girl, below the age of adulthood
Her action is nothing; it has no legal effect

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
From the fact that it teaches: the action of a young girl is nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for רפרם's limitation in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רפרם's rule that a child's deals do not count when there is a guardian.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: אֵין מַעֲשֵׂה קְטַנָּה כְּלוּם.

steps.title: Maybe the rule only applies when there is a שליש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof. Perhaps the girl's action is ignored only because a שליש was specifically appointed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps where there is a שליש, it is different?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in רפרם's proof. Maybe the משנה ignores the girl's action only in its special case, where a שליש was put in charge of that specific money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה's rule depends on a שליש being appointed for this task, it would not prove anything about guardians in general. The proof for רפרם would then fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
A third party trusted to hold and manage money
It is different

phrases.english: But perhaps where there is a third-party trustee, it is different?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from אֵין מַעֲשֵׂה קְטַנָּה כְּלוּם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's case may be limited to a specially appointed שליש, so it may not teach a general rule about guardians.

steps.title: The wording of the משנה is too broad for that
steps.stepSummary: If the rule only applied because of the שליש, the משנה should have said 'the שליש does his job.' Instead it says 'her action is nothing.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let it teach: 'But with a young girl, the שליש should do what was entrusted to him.' What is meant by 'the action of a young girl is nothing'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by looking closely at the משנה's words. It argues that the משנה chose a broad phrase on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the point were only about the שליש, the natural wording would be 'the שליש carries out his job.' Instead the משנה focuses on the girl herself and says her action is nothing. That wording points to something about the girl, not about the שליש.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let it teach; it should have said
Was entrusted to a שליש

phrases.english: If so, let it teach:
'But with a young girl, the trustee should carry out'
'what was entrusted into his hand.'
What is meant by 'the action of a young girl is nothing'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the משנה's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The girl's act is ignored only because a שליש was appointed for this money.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה would then have said 'the שליש does his job.' Saying 'her action is nothing' shows the rule is about the girl herself.

steps.title: The rule applies in general
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that a קטנה's action is void even in general, not only in the special שליש case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: even in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up and confirms רפרם's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A child who has someone in charge of her affairs cannot make deals that count. This is true even outside the special case of a שליש holding specific money.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; we can conclude
In general, in ordinary cases

steps.whatToRemember: רפרם's rule stands. Young children's deals in movable things count only when they have no guardian. The proof is the משנה's broad phrase אֵין מַעֲשֵׂה קְטַנָּה כְּלוּם.

phrases.english: Learn from this: even in general.
phrases.notes: 'In general' means even without a specially appointed שליש for this matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the answer in step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A קטנה's actions have no effect when someone is in charge of her affairs. This supports רפרם.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing מציאת האשה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the sixth פרק, מציאת האשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'The Findings of a Woman.'
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional farewell said at the end of each פרק. It expresses the hope to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you
'The findings of a woman,' the name of the פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter 'The Findings of a Woman.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the last discussion.

steps.title: A husband forbids his wife from benefiting from him
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens: if a husband makes a נדר forbidding his wife from benefiting from him, he appoints a פרנס for up to thirty days. For longer, he must divorce her and pay her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who vows to forbid his wife from benefiting from him: for up to thirty days, he appoints a provider. For longer than that, he must divorce her and give her the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה. It is about a husband whose נדר stops his wife from getting any benefit from him, including her food and support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a short time, the problem is solved by appointing a פרנס, an outside person who supports her instead of the husband. If the נדר lasts longer than thirty days, this is too hard on her. He must divorce her and pay her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who places someone under a נדר (vow)
To benefit
A provider or trustee who supports her
He must divorce her and pay her כתובה

steps.confusionAlert: The husband's נדר does not take away his duty to support her. He still owes her support, but he cannot give it directly. That is why a פרנס is needed.

phrases.english: One who vows, binding his wife,
so she may not benefit from him,
for up to thirty days, he must appoint a provider.
phrases.notes: The פרנס is someone else who gives her what she needs, so the benefit does not come straight from the husband.

phrases.english: More than this —
he must divorce her and give her the marriage contract payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Up to 30 days, he appoints a פרנס. Longer than that, he must divorce her and pay her כתובה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: different limits for a ישראל and a כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a ישראל may keep her for one month but must divorce at two. A כהן may keep her for two months but must divorce at three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: for a ישראל, one month he may keep her, two months he must divorce her and give the כתובה. For a כהן, two months he may keep her, three months he must divorce her and give the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה. He gives his own time limits, which depend on whether the husband is a regular ישראל or a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה allows a regular husband one month before divorce is required. He gives a כהן an extra month. A כהן may not remarry a divorced woman, even his own ex-wife, so a divorce would be permanent for him.

keyTerms.meaning: He may keep her as his wife
A regular Jew who is not a כהן
A priest, who may not marry a divorcée

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a halachic time limit can depend on how serious a divorce would be. For a כהן, a divorce could never be undone.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
With an Israelite: one month, he may keep her;
and two months, he must divorce her and give the marriage contract payment.
With a priest: two months, he may keep her;
and three months, he must divorce her and give the marriage contract payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing opinion to the first ruling of the משנה in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישראל: one month he may keep her, two months he must divorce. כהן: two months he may keep her, three months he must divorce.

steps.title: A vow forbidding the wife to taste a certain fruit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a husband who forbids his wife from tasting even one kind of fruit must divorce her and pay her כתובה. רבי יהודה gives a day-based limit: one day for a ישראל and two days for a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a husband makes a נדר that his wife may not taste even one kind of fruit, he must divorce her and pay her כתובה. רבי יהודה says: for a ישראל, if the vow lasts one day he may keep her, but if it lasts two days he must divorce her and pay. For a כהן, two days he may keep her, three days he must divorce her and pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new kind of vow: the husband forbids his wife from eating a certain fruit. The תנא קמא says he must divorce her, and רבי יהודה sets a short limit counted in days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even one forbidden fruit is enough to require divorce in the view of the first opinion. רבי יהודה softens this by allowing a very short vow: one day for a ישראל, two days for a כהן. Note that here the counting is in days, while in the earlier case of the משנה it was in months.

keyTerms.meaning: She will taste
Any one of all the fruits (even a single kind)
One day
Three (days)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with Step 13! There, רבי יהודה counted in MONTHS (for a vow against benefiting from the husband). Here the same structure is counted in DAYS (for a vow about food).

phrases.english: One who makes a vow against his wife
that she may not taste any one of all the fruits
must divorce her and give her the כתובה,
Rabbi Yehuda says:
For a Yisrael: one day, he may keep her;
two days, he must divorce her and give the כתובה.
And for a kohen: two days, he may keep her;
three days, he must divorce her and give the כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a second type of restrictive vow, following the same pattern as Steps 12–13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow forbidding the wife any one fruit requires divorce and payment of the כתובה. רבי יהודה allows one day for a ישראל and two days for a כהן.

steps.title: A vow forbidding the wife to adorn herself
steps.stepSummary: A husband who forbids his wife from adorning herself with any kind of adornment must divorce her and pay her כתובה. רבי יוסי distinguishes between poor women and wealthy women.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a husband makes a נדר that his wife may not adorn herself with even one kind of adornment, he must divorce her and pay her כתובה. רבי יוסי says: for poor women, this applies only when he set no time limit. For wealthy women, it applies at thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third kind of vow: the husband forbids his wife from using a certain kind of adornment. רבי יוסי adds that the rule depends on whether the woman is poor or wealthy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a poor woman, who adorns herself less, divorce is required only if the vow has no end date. For a wealthy woman, who is used to adorning herself more, a vow of thirty days is already enough to require divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: She will adorn herself
Kinds (types of adornment)
Poverty (here: poor women)
Wealth (here: wealthy women)
A set limit or fixed time

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה lists three vows: no benefit from the husband, no tasting a fruit, and no adornment. Each one requires divorce and payment of the כתובה, with time limits that vary by opinion.

phrases.english: One who makes a vow against his wife
that she may not adorn herself with any one of all the kinds
must divorce her and give the כתובה.
Rabbi Yosei says:
For poor women: when he did not set a time limit;
and for wealthy women: thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the third and final case of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow forbidding adornment requires divorce. רבי יוסי says that for poor women this applies only when no time limit was set, and for wealthy women it applies at thirty days.

steps.title: How can a husband's vow cancel his duty to support her?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first case of the משנה. The husband is already obligated to support his wife, so how can his vow forbidding her to benefit from him work at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But since he is already obligated to support her, how can he make a vow against her? Does he have the power to cancel his obligation to her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and immediately questions the very first ruling of the משנה (Step 12). It asks how the husband's vow can take effect when he already owes her support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband takes on a duty to support his wife when they marry. A person normally cannot use a נדר to get out of something he already owes someone else. So the משנה's assumption that his vow works, even needing a פרנס, seems puzzling.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows and explains the משנה
Obligated, bound by a duty
An existing obligation or lien
Is it in his power?
Cancels, removes

phrases.english: GEMARA: But since he is obligated to her,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the first case of the משנה, where he forbade her from benefiting from him.

phrases.english: how can he make a vow against her?
Is it in his power
to cancel his obligation to her?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן דִּמְשׁוּעְבַּד לָהּ הֵיכִי מָצֵי מַדִּיר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by attacking the basic assumption of the first case in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's assumption (Step 12) that a husband's vow forbidding his wife from benefiting from him takes effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He already owes her support, and a person cannot use a vow to cancel an existing obligation to someone else.

steps.title: Proof from a wife who vows not to work for her husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its challenge with a משנה in נדרים. A wife's vow not to work for her husband does not take effect, because she already owes him that work. The same should be true of the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn: if a wife says 'It is קונם that I will not work for your mouth,' the husband does not need to cancel her vow. This shows that since she is obligated to him, she does not have the power to cancel her obligation to him. Here too, since he is obligated to her, he should not have the power to cancel his obligation to her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to strengthen its question from Step 16. It shows that in the reverse case, a wife cannot use a vow to escape her duty to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In נדרים, a wife's vow not to work for her husband simply does not take effect, so he does not even need to cancel it. The reason is that she already owes him that work. The גמרא applies the same logic in reverse: the husband owes her support, so his vow should not work either.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow formula making something forbidden like a קרבן
To cancel (a husband canceling his wife's vow)
This shows, evidently
Here too

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the central puzzle of the sugya: a vow cannot cancel an existing obligation, yet the משנה treats the husband's vow as effective. The גמרא will need to explain how.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the question of Step 16 with a משנה that shows the same principle.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge that a husband's vow cannot cancel his existing obligation to support his wife.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in נדרים 85a: a wife's vow not to work for her husband does not take effect, because she is already obligated to him.

steps.title: The husband can tell her to support herself from her earnings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer the challenge. A husband has the right to say to his wife, 'Keep your earnings and use them for your food.' So his duty to support her is not fixed in a way that blocks his vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since he is able to say to her, 'Go out with your earnings in place of your food.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting its answer to the question of how the husband's vow can work. This line sets up the reason, and the conclusion comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in Step 16 assumed the husband is fully bound to feed his wife, so he cannot vow her out of it, just as her vow in Step 17 could not cancel work she owes him. The new point is that the husband can at any time switch the arrangement: she keeps her own earnings and feeds herself from them. Because of that option, his support duty is not locked in the way her work duty is, which opens the door for his vow to take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the גמרא is now giving a new explanation.
Since, or because. It introduces the reason behind a ruling.
Go out. Here it means 'be on your own' or 'manage for yourself.'
Your handiwork, meaning your earnings from your own work.
Your food, meaning the support the husband normally gives his wife.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the full answer. It only gives the reason ('since he can say...'). The conclusion about the vow comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer depends on the basic deal between husband and wife: he feeds her, and her earnings go to him. Because he can choose to end that deal, his duty to support her is different from her duty to work for him.

phrases.english: Rather: since he is able to say to her
"Go out with your earnings in place of your food,"
phrases.notes: Literally 'go out, your handiwork for your food.' He means: keep what you earn and feed yourself with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 16, which Step 17 backed up with the משנה in נדרים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the husband's support duty from the wife's work duty: he can end his duty by giving her own earnings to her.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The husband's duty to feed his wife is fixed, just like her duty to work for him, so his vow should not take effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the husband can tell her to feed herself from her earnings, his support duty is not fixed in the same way, which sets up how his vow can work.
